blogs.title: Beyond the Bite: Unmasking Complement-Mediated HUS After Capnocytophaga Sepsis
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing between sepsis-induced Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) and secondary Thrombotic Microangiopathy (TMA). We analyze how C. canimorsus can act as a 'trigger' for Complement-Mediated Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (CM-HUS) in immunocompetent adults, discussing why hemolysis and thrombocytopenia may worsen only after the initial septic shock appears to resolve.

blogs.title: The Normal C3/C4 Trap: Why Standard Labs Miss Atypical HUS
blogs.description: A deep dive into the limitations of routine complement screening. We explain why normal C3 and C4 levels do not rule out CM-HUS, contrasting the pathophysiology of alternative pathway dysregulation with classic consumption patterns seen in other conditions. This piece guides clinicians on interpreting negative autoimmune panels and normal complement levels in the face of clear Microangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia (MAHA).

blogs.title: Eculizumab vs. Active Bacteremia: Navigating the Therapeutic Paradox
blogs.description: Addressing one of the most complex dilemmas in critical care nephrology: when to initiate terminal complement blockade in a patient with recent or resolving bacteremia. We review the specific risks of eculizumab regarding encapsulated organisms like *Neisseria* and *Capnocytophaga*, outlining a safe protocol involving blood culture clearance, aggressive vaccination strategies, and antimicrobial prophylaxis before dosing.

blogs.title: ADAMTS13 >10% and Schistocytes Present: The Algorithm for Adult TMA
blogs.description: A practical guide to triaging adult patients with MAHA, thrombocytopenia, and AKI. Using this case as a template, we walk through the decision tree to distinguish TTP (PLASMIC score utility), STEC-HUS (stool PCR necessity), and CM-HUS. Special emphasis is placed on recognizing that Plasma Exchange (PEX) serves as a bridge therapy in CM-HUS but is not curative compared to targeted complement inhibition.

blogs.title: Genetic Luck vs. Environmental Trigger: Acquired CM-HUS Without Mutations
blogs.description: Discussing the evolving understanding of CM-HUS genetics. Unlike typical 'atypical HUS' cases driven by germline mutations in Factor H or I, this case illustrates 'infection-triggered' CM-HUS where no pathogenic variants were found. We explore the concept that severe environmental insults alone can unleash complement dysregulation and discuss how this impacts long-term prognostication and duration of eculizumab therapy.
